page.overview:
What is Pikachu?

Pikachu is renowned for being the most well-known and recognizable Pokémon. Over the years, Pikachu has become so popular that it serves as the Pokémon mascot. In the games, Pikachu is the version mascot and first partner Pokémon of and its remake . In the anime, Pikachu appeared regularly as the main travel companion and partner to Ash Ketchum; while another variant, partners alongside Professor Friede in .

Pikachu is a small, plump, mouse-like Pokémon almost completely covered in yellow fur. Its face has brown eyes, a small mouth, and circular red cheek pouches where it stores electricity. It has long, pointed ears with black markings at the tips. Pikachu has short arms with five tiny fingers on each forepaw and three sharp toes on each hind foot. It has two brown stripes on its back, and its large tail is shaped like a lightning bolt. Pikachu turns yellow and sparks with electricity when it is about to use an -type move, such as Thunderbolt. Despite being categorized as a quadruped, Pikachu often stands and moves upright on two legs. One of the smaller design details with Pikachu is that it has a patch of brown fur at the base of its tail.

A female Pikachu looks almost exactly the same as a male, with the exception of her tail, which is rounded at the end and has an inward dent, giving it the appearance of a heart. However, in earlier episodes of and in the games prior to Generation IV, female and male Pikachu look identical, as gender differences had not yet been introduced for Pokémon.

As Gigantamax Pikachu, it becomes larger and chubbier, similar to its Generation I design. Its tail becomes longer and stores all of the electricity it generates, causing it to glow a bright yellow and enabling it to become as powerful as a lightning strike. Its power is equal to that of a power plant; however, it is difficult to use in people's homes, since Pikachu can only remain in its Gigantamax form for a short time.
